stem: In modern periodic table the non-metals are found in ______.
solution:
**(B)** p-block

The elements of groups 13 to 18 form the p-block of the modern periodic table, and this block contains metals, non-metals and metalloids. Apart from hydrogen, every non-metal lies in the p-block. The s-block, d-block and f-block elements are all metals (hydrogen excepted). \(\therefore\) The non-metals are found in the p-block.

stem:
\(CuSO_{4(aq)} + Zn_{(s)} \longrightarrow ZnSO_{4(aq)} + Cu_{(s)}\).

This is ______ type of chemical reaction.
solution:
**(A)** displacement

Zinc is more reactive than copper. It displaces the copper ion from copper sulphate solution, so zinc goes into solution as zinc sulphate and copper metal is deposited. A reaction in which the place of the ion of a less reactive element in a compound is taken by a more reactive element is a displacement reaction. Only one exchange takes place here, so it is not a double displacement.

stem: The unit of electric power is ______.
solution:
**(C)** Watt

Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is used: \(P = \frac{W}{t} = VI\). Its SI unit is joule per second, which is called the watt: 1 watt = 1 volt \(\times\) 1 ampere. Joule is the unit of energy, volt of potential difference and coulomb of charge.

stem: We can see the sun even when it is little below the horizon because of ______.
solution:
**(B)** refraction of light

The refractive index of the atmosphere increases towards the earth's surface. Light from the sun, when it is slightly below the horizon, bends continuously as it passes through these layers (atmospheric refraction) and reaches us along a curved path. So the sun appears above the horizon and we keep seeing it for a short while even after it has gone below the horizon.

stem: ______ is one of the combustible component of L.P.G.
solution:
**(B)** Propane

L.P.G. (liquefied petroleum gas) is mainly a mixture of propane (\(C_3H_8\)) and butane, and propane is one of its combustible components. On complete combustion: \(C_3H_8 + 5O_2 \rightarrow 3CO_2 + 4H_2O\) + heat. Methane is the main component of CNG and biogas, not of L.P.G.

Write the correlation:

Brass : Copper and Zinc :: Bronze : ______
solution: Brass : Copper and Zinc :: Bronze : **Copper and Tin**. Bronze is an alloy of copper (90%) and tin (10%).

stem:
Write True or False:

Benzene is an aromatic compound.
solution: True. Benzene (\(C_6H_6\)) is a cyclic unsaturated hydrocarbon with three alternate double bonds in its six-membered ring. Compounds having this characteristic unit in their structure are called aromatic compounds.

subtopic: Human Eye and Defects of Vision
stem:
Find the odd one out:

Myopia; Presbyopia; Hypermetropia; Retina
solution: Retina is the odd one out. Myopia, presbyopia and hypermetropia are defects of vision, whereas the retina is a part of the eye (the light-sensitive screen on which the image is formed).

stem: What is angle of refraction when angle of incidence is \(0^\circ\)?
solution: The angle of refraction is \(0^\circ\). When the angle of incidence is \(0^\circ\), the ray falls along the normal, and a ray incident along the normal passes into the second medium without bending (\(\sin r = \frac{\sin 0^\circ}{n} = 0\)).

stem: Name two appliances which work on the principle of magnetic effect of electric current.
solution: (1) Electric motor (2) Galvanometer. In both, a current-carrying coil placed in a magnetic field experiences a force and rotates.

stem: Give scientific reason: Sodium is always kept in kerosene.
solution: Sodium is a highly reactive metal. On exposure to air it reacts vigorously with oxygen and moisture and readily catches fire: \(4Na_{(s)} + O_{2(g)} \rightarrow 2Na_2O_{(s)}\). Sodium does not react with kerosene, and the kerosene keeps air and moisture away from it. Therefore, to prevent accidents in the laboratory or elsewhere, sodium is always kept in kerosene.

stem: Give scientific reason: A simple microscope is used for watch repairs.
solution: A simple microscope is a convex lens of small focal length. When a small object is placed within its focal length, it forms a virtual, erect and magnified image (up to about 20 times larger) of the object. The parts of a watch are very small, so the watch repairer uses a simple microscope to see these minute parts clearly in magnified form while repairing them.

stem: Give scientific reason: It is necessary to manage the space debris.
solution: Space debris consists of non-functional satellites, parts of launchers detached during launching and pieces formed by collisions of satellites with other objects, all revolving around the earth. This debris can collide with working artificial satellites and spacecrafts and damage them. The debris is increasing day by day, and soon it will be difficult to launch new spacecrafts safely. Therefore it is necessary to manage the space debris.

stem: The absolute refractive index of water is 1.33. What is the velocity of light in water? (Velocity of light in vacuum \(= 3 \times 10^8\) m/s)
solution:
Given: absolute refractive index of water \(n = 1.33\), velocity of light in vacuum \(c = 3 \times 10^8\) m/s. To find: velocity of light in water \(v\).

Formula: \(n = \frac{c}{v}\), so \(v = \frac{c}{n}\).

\(v = \frac{3 \times 10^8\ \text{m/s}}{1.33}\)

\(\therefore v \approx 2.26 \times 10^8\) m/s.

Check: \(1.33 \times 2.26 \times 10^8 \approx 3.0 \times 10^8\) m/s, and the speed in water is less than in vacuum, as it must be.

The velocity of light in water is about \(2.26 \times 10^8\) m/s.

subtopic: Latent Heat and Change of State

Observe the figure and answer the questions given below.

(a) Name the phenomenon shown in the figure.
(b) Define the above phenomenon.
solution:
(a) The phenomenon shown is regelation (a metal wire with weights hung at its ends passes through the ice slab without breaking it).

(b) Regelation: The phenomenon in which ice converts to liquid due to applied pressure and then re-converts to ice once the pressure is removed is called regelation. stem:
Observe the reaction below, in which the changes A and B are marked:

\(2H_2S + SO_2 \longrightarrow 3S\downarrow + 2H_2O\)

(a) Identify the above chemical reaction.
(b) Name the type of reaction in A and B.
solution:
(a) It is a redox reaction: oxidation and reduction take place simultaneously.

(b) A (\(SO_2 \rightarrow S\)): sulphur dioxide loses oxygen to form sulphur, so A is a reduction reaction.
B (\(H_2S \rightarrow H_2O\)): the hydrogen of hydrogen sulphide takes up oxygen and forms water (\(H_2S\) loses hydrogen and becomes sulphur), so B is an oxidation reaction.

\(H_2S\) is the reductant and \(SO_2\) is the oxidant; Redox reaction = Reduction + Oxidation.
figureNote: the equation 2H2S + SO2 -> 3S(down) + 2H2O with bracket arrow A above (from SO2 to 3S) and bracket arrow B below (from 2H2S to 2H2O), p-04

stem:
Define the following terms:

(a) Escape velocity
(b) Free fall.
solution:
(a) Escape velocity: The minimum initial velocity with which an object must be thrown vertically upwards from the surface of the earth so that it overcomes the earth's gravitational pull and escapes the earth forever (never falls back) is called escape velocity. \(v_{esc} = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}\), about 11.2 km/s for the earth.

(b) Free fall: When an object moves under the influence of the force of gravity alone, it is said to be falling freely, i.e. it is in free fall. True free fall is possible only in vacuum, since air exerts friction and a buoyant force on a falling object.

stem:
What information will you get from the given reaction?

\(CaCO_{3(s)} \xrightarrow{\Delta} CaO_{(s)} + CO_2\uparrow\)
solution:
(1) Reactant: calcium carbonate (limestone), in the solid state (s).
(2) Products: calcium oxide (quicklime) in the solid state, and carbon dioxide, a gas (shown by the upward arrow).
(3) The sign \(\Delta\) above the arrow shows that heat has to be supplied from outside, so it is an endothermic reaction.
(4) One reactant breaks down into two simpler products, so it is a decomposition (thermal decomposition) reaction.
(5) The equation is balanced: one molecule of \(CaCO_3\) gives one molecule of \(CaO\) and one molecule of \(CO_2\) (1 Ca, 1 C and 3 O atoms on each side).

stem:
Observe the following ray diagram and answer the questions given below:

(a) Identify the instrument shown in the diagram.
(b) What is the combined effect of two lenses?
(c) Write the use of the above instrument.
solution:
(a) The instrument is a compound microscope (two convex lenses: the objective lens and the eyepiece).

(b) The magnification occurs in two stages. The objective (small focal length) forms a real, inverted and magnified image of the object; this image acts as the object for the eyepiece, which forms a final virtual and further magnified image. The combined effect of the two lenses is a much higher magnification than a single lens (simple microscope) can give.

(c) A compound microscope is used to study minute objects such as blood cells, cells of plants and animals, and minute living beings like bacteria, which a simple microscope cannot magnify sufficiently.

stem:
Read the following paragraph and answer the questions given below:

Rainbow is a beautiful natural phenomenon. It is the combined effect of dispersion, refraction and total internal reflection of light. It can be seen mainly after rainfall. Small droplets of water act as small prisms. When light rays from the sun enter these droplets it gets refracted and dispersed. Then there is internal reflection and after that once again the light gets refracted while coming out of the droplet. All these three processes together produce the rainbow.

(a) Which three major phenomena are responsible for rainbow formation?
(b) How does refraction take place?
(c) Draw a diagrammatic representation of rainbow production.
solution:
(a) Dispersion of light, refraction of light and total internal reflection of light.

(b) When sunlight passes from air into a water droplet, its speed changes, so it bends (is refracted) at the surface of the droplet; since the droplet acts like a small prism, the different colours bend by different amounts and the light is also dispersed. After internal reflection at the back of the droplet, the light is refracted once again while coming out of the droplet into air.

(c) Diagram of rainbow production (to be drawn and labelled): a circular water droplet; a ray of white sunlight entering it at the upper surface and refracting, splitting into colours from violet to red; the coloured rays reflected internally at the back surface of the droplet; the rays refracting again as they leave the droplet towards the observer, with red and violet labelled on the emerging rays. Labels: sunlight, water droplet, refraction and dispersion, internal reflection, refraction, red, violet.

(a) Name the elements in which both the shells are completely filled with electrons.
(b) Name the element which has same number of electrons in both the shells.
(c) Which is the most electropositive element in this period?
solution:
Electronic configurations: Li (2,1), Be (2,2), B (2,3), C (2,4), N (2,5), O (2,6), F (2,7), Ne (2,8).

(a) Neon (Ne, 2,8): both its K shell (2 electrons) and L shell (8 electrons) are completely filled. It is the only such element in the second period.

(b) Beryllium (Be, 2,2): it has 2 electrons in each of its two shells.

(c) Lithium (Li): it has only one valence electron, which it loses most easily. Electropositivity (metallic character) decreases from left to right across a period, so lithium is the most electropositive element of the second period.

subtopic: Free Fall and Acceleration due to Gravity
stem: Explain on which factor the value of acceleration due to gravity 'g' depends.
solution:
From Newton's law of gravitation, \(g = \frac{GM}{r^2}\), where \(M\) is the mass of the earth and \(r\) is the distance of the object from the centre of the earth. So \(g\) depends on the mass of the earth and on the distance from its centre, and not on the mass or other properties of the object. Hence it varies as follows:

(1) Along the surface of the earth: the earth bulges at the equator and is flatter at the poles, so its radius is largest at the equator. \(g\) is highest at the poles (\(9.832\) m/s\(^2\)) and lowest at the equator (\(9.78\) m/s\(^2\)).
(2) With height: as we go above the earth's surface, \(r\) increases and \(g\) decreases.
(3) With depth: as we go inside the earth, the part of the earth's mass that attracts the object decreases, so \(g\) decreases (it is zero at the centre).

stem:
Explain the following terms:

(a) Metallurgy
(b) Ores
(c) Gangue.
solution:
(a) Metallurgy: The science and technology regarding the extraction of metals from their ores and their purification for use is called metallurgy.

(b) Ores: The minerals from which a metal can be separated economically are called ores. For example, bauxite is an ore of aluminium.

(c) Gangue: Ores contain many types of impurities such as soil, sand and rocky substances along with the metal compounds. These impurities are called gangue. They are separated from the ore during concentration of the ore.

stem:
(a) What is meant by anomalous behaviour of water?
(b) Explain the role of anomalous behaviour of water in preserving aquatic life in cold climate.
solution:
(a) Generally a liquid expands on heating and contracts on cooling. Water, however, contracts instead of expanding when it is heated from \(0^\circ\)C to \(4^\circ\)C; its volume is minimum (density maximum) at \(4^\circ\)C, and above \(4^\circ\)C it expands. This exceptional behaviour of water between \(0^\circ\)C and \(4^\circ\)C is called the anomalous behaviour of water.

(b) In cold regions, as the air temperature falls, the surface water of a lake cools, becomes denser and sinks, and warmer water rises. This continues until the whole water body is at \(4^\circ\)C. On further cooling, the surface water below \(4^\circ\)C becomes lighter, so it stays at the top and finally freezes at \(0^\circ\)C. Ice is a poor conductor of heat, so the layer of ice prevents the water below from cooling further, and the water at the bottom remains at about \(4^\circ\)C. Hence aquatic plants and animals survive even when the atmospheric temperature goes below \(0^\circ\)C.

stem:
Observe the following diagram and answer the questions given below:

(a) Identify the above diagram.
(b) Write the principle on which the above appliance works.
(c) Write the working of the above appliance.
(d) Write the use of the above appliance.
solution:
(a) The diagram shows an AC generator (alternating current generator).

(b) Principle: electromagnetic induction. When a coil rotates in a magnetic field, the magnetic field linked with it changes and an electric current is induced in the coil.

(c) Working: The copper coil ABCD is kept between the poles N and S of a magnet. Its two ends are connected to the conducting rings \(R_1\) and \(R_2\), which are fixed to the axle, and the stationary carbon brushes \(B_1\) and \(B_2\) connect the rings to a galvanometer. The axle is rotated from outside by a machine. When branch AB goes up and branch CD goes down, by Fleming's right hand rule current flows A to B to C to D, and in the external circuit from \(B_2\) to \(B_1\) through the galvanometer. After half a rotation, AB and CD exchange places, so the induced current flows D to C to B to A, and in the external circuit from \(B_1\) to \(B_2\). Since each branch always stays in contact with the same brush, the direction of current in the external circuit reverses every half rotation, and alternating current is produced.

(d) Use: The AC generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. It is used in power stations to produce the alternating current supplied to homes and industries.
figureNote: AC generator: coil ABCD between magnet poles N and S (magnetic field arrow), conducting rings R1 R2 on the axle, carbon brushes B1 B2, external circuit with galvanometer G, p-09

stem:
Read the following paragraph and answer the questions given below:

Carbon compounds contain many elements. The element hydrogen is present to a smaller or larger extent in majority of carbon compounds. The compounds which contain carbon and hydrogen as the only two elements are called hydrocarbons. Hydrocarbons are the simplest and the fundamental organic compounds. The smallest hydrocarbon is methane (\(CH_4\)), formed by combination of one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms. We have already seen the structure of methane. Ethane is one more hydrocarbon. Its molecular formula is \(C_2H_6\).

The carbon compounds having a double bond or triple bond between two carbon atoms are called unsaturated compounds. Ethene and ethyne are unsaturated hydrocarbons. The unsaturated hydrocarbons containing a carbon-carbon double bond are called 'Alkenes'. The unsaturated hydrocarbons whose structures contain a carbon-carbon triple bond are called 'Alkynes'. Generally the unsaturated compounds are more reactive than the saturated compounds.

(a) What is meant by hydrocarbon?
(b) Name the smallest hydrocarbon.
(c) Define unsaturated compound.
(d) Differentiate between Alkene and Alkyne.
solution:
(a) The compounds which contain carbon and hydrogen as the only two elements are called hydrocarbons.

(b) Methane (\(CH_4\)) is the smallest hydrocarbon.

(c) The carbon compounds having a double bond or a triple bond between two carbon atoms are called unsaturated compounds.

(d)

| Alkene | Alkyne |
|---|---|
| An unsaturated hydrocarbon containing a carbon-carbon double bond (\(C=C\)). | An unsaturated hydrocarbon containing a carbon-carbon triple bond (\(C \equiv C\)). |
| General formula \(C_nH_{2n}\). | General formula \(C_nH_{2n-2}\). |
| Name ends in -ene. | Name ends in -yne. |
| Example: ethene (\(C_2H_4\)). | Example: ethyne (\(C_2H_2\)). |
